- brainstorming: You MUST use this before any creative work - creating features, building components, adding functionality, or modifying behavior. Explores user intent, requirements and design before implementation.
- coding-standards: Baseline cross-project coding conventions for naming, readability, immutability, and code-quality review. Use detailed frontend or backend skills for framework-specific patterns.
- dispatching-parallel-agents: Use when facing 2+ independent tasks that can be worked on without shared state or sequential dependencies
- executing-plans: Use when you have a written implementation plan to execute in a separate session with review checkpoints
- finishing-a-development-branch: Use when implementation is complete, all tests pass, and you need to decide how to integrate the work - guides completion of development work by presenting structured options for merge, PR, or cleanup
- open-design--baseline-ui: Quickly deslop UI code by fixing spacing, hierarchy, typography, and small layout issues. Use when the interface needs a fast cleanup or polish pass.
- open-design--fixing-accessibility: Audit and fix HTML accessibility issues including ARIA labels, keyboard navigation, focus management, color contrast, and form errors. Use when adding interactive controls, forms, dialogs, or reviewing WCAG compliance.
- open-design--fixing-metadata: Audit and fix HTML metadata including page titles, meta descriptions, canonical URLs, Open Graph tags, Twitter cards, favicons, JSON-LD structured data, and robots directives. Use when adding SEO metadata, fixing social share previews, reviewing Open Graph tags, setting up canonical URLs, or shipping new pages that need correct meta tags.
- open-design--fixing-motion-performance: Audit and fix animation performance issues including layout thrashing, compositor properties, scroll-linked motion, and blur effects. Use when animations stutter, transitions jank, or reviewing CSS/JS animation performance.
- open-design--frontend-design: Guidance for distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI or reshaping an existing one. Helps with aesthetic direction, typography, and making choices that don't read as templated defaults.
- open-design--frontend-slides: Create stunning, animation-rich HTML presentations from scratch or by converting PowerPoint files. Use when the user wants to build a presentation, convert a PPT/PPTX to web, or create slides for a talk/pitch. Helps non-designers discover their aesthetic through visual exploration rather than abstract choices.
- open-design--theme-factory: Toolkit for styling artifacts with a theme. These artifacts can be slides, docs, reportings, HTML landing pages, etc. There are 10 pre-set themes with colors/fonts that you can apply to any artifact that has been creating, or can generate a new theme on-the-fly.
- receiving-code-review: Use when receiving code review feedback, before implementing suggestions, especially if feedback seems unclear or technically questionable - requires technical rigor and verification, not performative agreement or blind implementation
- requesting-code-review: Use when completing tasks, implementing major features, or before merging to verify work meets requirements
- security-review: Use this skill when adding authentication, handling user input, working with secrets, creating API endpoints, or implementing payment/sensitive features. Provides comprehensive security checklist and patterns.
- subagent-driven-development: Use when executing implementation plans with independent tasks in the current session
- submit-artifact: Use when submitting any Ralph Workflow artifact as a markdown document via ralph_submit_md_artifact, when pre-checking a draft with ralph_verify_md_artifact, or when a submission returned diagnostics with codes like MD001-MD007, SPEC001-SPEC012, or REF001-REF004 and you need the closed markdown grammar
- submit-commit-cleanup-artifact: Use when submitting a commit_cleanup artifact as markdown via ralph_submit_md_artifact with delete_file / add_to_gitignore / add_to_git_exclude actions, or when an action was rejected by the printable-ASCII rule or silently dropped by the security boundary
- submit-commit-message-artifact: Use when submitting a commit_message artifact as markdown via ralph_submit_md_artifact with a commit or skip frontmatter variant, or when the conventional-commit subject was rejected and you need the exact subject rule
- submit-development-result-artifact: Use when submitting a development_result artifact as markdown via ralph_submit_md_artifact with ID-based proof entries in Plan Items Proven and Analysis Items Addressed, or when a completed result was rejected for a missing section or an unproven plan or analysis item
- submit-plan-artifact: Use when authoring or revising a markdown plan artifact
- systematic-debugging: Use when encountering any bug, test failure, or unexpected behavior, before proposing fixes
- test-driven-development: Use when implementing any feature or bugfix, before writing implementation code
- using-git-worktrees: Use when starting feature work that needs isolation from current workspace or before executing implementation plans - ensures an isolated workspace exists via native tools or git worktree fallback
- using-superpowers: Use when starting any conversation - establishes how to find and use skills, requiring skill invocation before ANY response including clarifying questions
- verification-before-completion: Use when about to claim work is complete, fixed, or passing, before committing or creating PRs - requires running verification commands and confirming output before making any success claims; evidence before assertions always
- verification-loop: A comprehensive verification system for Claude Code sessions.
- writing-plans: Use when planning a multi-step change before editing code
- writing-skills: Use when creating new skills, editing existing skills, or verifying skills work before deployment
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

default structure; it does not require a uniform document. A step may use
`### [S-n] Title`; IDs are stable and never renumbered when your plan needs
them. Use `Type: verify` for a test-running step when useful; step types are
preserved verbatim. `PLAN001` is the only blocking plan diagnostic: the submission is empty, too short, or plainly
not a plan. Warnings and info are advice. Record a normal, reasoned decision
to proceed past advice under `## Validation Overrides`; tool results retain
those reasons.

Submit a complete plan with `mcp__ralph__ralph_submit_md_artifact`
(`artifact_type="plan"`). For a similar revision, use

validates. Use `mcp__ralph__ralph_stage_md_artifact` with `mode="replace_all"`
only for a wholesale rewrite. `mcp__ralph__ralph_get_md_draft` shows the draft,
and `mcp__ralph__ralph_finalize_md_artifact` submits an assembled staged draft.
Staging alone does not persist a plan: a draft that differs from the submitted
document blocks phase completion until you resubmit it or deliberately discard
it with `ralph_discard_md_draft`. Do not write canonical plan files directly. After a valid receipt, call
`mcp__ralph__declare_complete` as the final action.

# Contractor surface — change batch 1

Work the contractor course-plan builder through the spec below. Read `AGENTS.md`
and the policies in `docs/ralph-workflow-policy/` before changing anything, and
use `make verify` as the authoritative gate before claiming any item done.

Each item gives the request **verbatim**, the **decision** taken on it, and
**acceptance criteria**. Where the original request was ambiguous, the decision
records the call and the reasoning. Do not widen scope past these criteria; if
an item turns out to be wrong, say so rather than silently redesigning it.

Two screenshots accompany this batch:

- **Screenshot A** — the course plan builder today: the
  `within 2 weeks students will be able to…` watermark, the course/round context
  line, the milestone and activity boxes, and the current placement of the move
  up / move down / delete controls. Most layout items below describe this screen.
- **Screenshot B** — milestone vs activity type hierarchy, for the font item.

## What already exists (do not rebuild)

Verified in the codebase before writing this spec:

- **Activity minutes already exist.** `course_plan_activities.time_value_min`
  (integer, default 0, not null). `_course_milestone.html.erb` already renders
  `"… min in this milestone"`, and `CoursePlan#recompute_totals!` already
  maintains `course_plan.totals_min` (excluding `synthesis` activities).
- **AI assist already exists.** `app/views/shared/plan_builder/_ai_assist.html.erb`
  — a modal with a plan prompt, Generate, and replace / amend / append apply
  modes, driven by the `plan-ai-assist` Stimulus controller.
- **Move up / Move down / Delete already exist** in `_course_milestone.html.erb`.
- **Plan editability is already governed by status**, not schedule:
  `CoursePlan#editable?` is `draft? || needs_revision?`, enforced in
  `CoursePlanMilestonesController#load_course_plan`.
- **The LLM stack is provider-generic.** `Llm::Client` is the single chat
  transport seam and resolves the active provider at call time from
  `SiteAiSetting` / `OrganizationAiSetting`, so a SUP can switch providers
  without code changes. `SiteAiSetting::SUPPORTED_PROVIDERS` is
  `%w[openai gemini]`, `AiCredential` already holds credentials for both
  (`openai_api_key` / `openai_api_base` and the Vertex AI service-account
  fields), and `LlmModelCatalogEntry` carries a `provider` column. **No item in
  this batch should name or add a specific provider** — anything AI-facing goes
  through the existing seam and works with whichever provider is configured.

## Checklist

### 1. Milestone add / reorder is broken

> **Adding Milestones and moving them up or down in the plan is broken. Please
> make operations …**

The request is cut off mid-sentence. Rather than guess the missing clause, the
behaviour was diagnosed directly. **Three independent root causes**, all real:

1. **Mixed position bases.** `next_position`
   (`CoursePlanMilestonesController:131`) returns `maximum(:position).to_i + 1`,
   so the *first* milestone in a plan gets position **1**. But
   `reorder_milestones!` (:142) and `restore` (:61) renormalise to a **0**-based
   dense index. A never-reordered plan is 1-based; one reorder silently converts
   it to 0-based. The "Move up" disabled check in the view is
   `milestone.position.zero?`, which never fires on a 1-based plan — so the
   first milestone shows an **enabled "Move up" button that does nothing**.
2. **`destroy` never renormalises.** It only sets `discarded_at`
   (:42–50), so positions develop gaps — `[0, 2, 3]`. The view computes
   `position - 1` / `position + 1` from the *stored* position, but
   `reorder_milestones!` treats the incoming number as an *index* into the
   ordered sibling list (`siblings.insert(target, …)`). Once positions have
   gaps, stored position ≠ index, so "Move up" from stored position 2 resolves
   to index 1 — where the milestone already sits. **No-op, or a two-slot jump.**
   `CoursePlanActivitiesController#destroy` has the identical defect.
3. **Turbo-frame lock staleness.** `respond_to_milestone_mutation` (:169)
   re-renders only the mutated milestone's frame, but
   `lock_course_plan_for_mutation` (:103) bumps the parent plan's `lock_version`
   on every successful mutation. Every *other* milestone frame still embeds the
   old `lock_version`, and `verify_course_plan_lock` (:87) rejects any mismatch
   — so the next click on a different milestone 409s with
   **"This plan changed in another session. Reload it and try again."**

**Decision:** make `position` a dense, 0-based index that is authoritative after
every mutation, and stop doing arithmetic on stored positions in the view.

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] `next_position` and the renormalise paths agree on a single 0-based
      convention. A plan's positions are always `0..n-1` with no gaps.
- [ ] `destroy` renormalises surviving siblings — milestones **and** activities.
- [ ] Move up / down send the target **index derived from the rendered order**,
      not `stored_position ± 1`.
- [ ] "Move up" is disabled on the first milestone and "Move down" on the last,
      including immediately after a delete.
- [ ] Two consecutive mutations on *different* milestones both succeed with no
      reload — no spurious stale-plan 409.
- [ ] Regression tests cover: reorder after delete, reorder on a fresh plan, and
      back-to-back mutations on different milestones.

### 2. Preround contractor

> **Preround Contractor. Are we in the round or before the round**

**Decision: informational and navigational only — not a second permission gate.**
Plan editability is already governed by plan status. Layering a schedule-based
lock on top creates states where a plan is `draft` (so the UI offers editing)
but blocked for schedule reasons, with no recovery path for the contractor.
Show *where we are*; let status keep deciding *what's allowed*.

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] Contractor surfaces show whether the round is before start or in progress.
- [ ] The state comes from `Round#student_start_state`
      (`:unknown` / `:future` / `:past`) — do not add a second predicate, and do
      not read `created_at` as schedule data.
- [ ] `:unknown` (no published schedule) renders no preround claim at all.
- [ ] No editing permission changes in this item.

### 3. Watermarks

> **Watermark within 2 weeks students will be able to…** (Screenshot A)
>
> **Also remove the "optional….purpose" watermark.**

The second is `app/views/contractor_course_plans/new.html.erb:34` —
`Optional. State what students will learn or make so the first milestone has a
clear purpose.`

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] Both watermarks removed from the course plan surface.
- [ ] Removing helper copy does not orphan an `aria-describedby` reference.

### 4. Ten capture boxes

> **Add an extension on the course plan page or 10 boxes that allow contractors
> to type in, upload or speak/LLM Generate**

**Decision: ten numbered source-material slots on the course plan page, each
accepting typed text, a file upload, or dictation, feeding the existing AI
assist as source material.** Reading "extension … or 10 boxes" as two names for
one feature, and "type in, upload or speak" as three input modes for a single
box rather than three separate features. They feed the existing
`plan_draft` apply pipeline instead of a parallel generator.

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] Ten slots on the course plan page, each supporting all three input modes.
- [ ] Slots may be left blank; empty slots contribute nothing.
- [ ] Contents feed the existing assist and land through the existing
      replace / amend / append modes.
- [ ] Uploads honour the accept-type and size limits already used by the guide
      import; dictation degrades gracefully where unsupported.
- [ ] Generation goes through the existing `Llm::Client` seam and behaves the
      same under whichever provider the site is configured for. No
      provider-specific branch, no new transport, no new credential fields.
- [ ] An unconfigured or disabled AI provider degrades to a clear message — the
      slots still accept typed text, uploads and dictation.

### 5. Plan builder layout

> **Would prefer the Milestone font bolded and larger than the activity font**
> (Screenshot B)
>
> **`## Biology AM / 2026 Early August — Round 1 — Spring Field Study / AM`
> Make that the light grey**
>
> **Second box is the milestone which expands to the the activities**
>
> **Move move up, move down and delete over to the right.**
>
> **Add Acitivity button that expands and collapses activities**
>
> **Default 1 Milestones and 2 activities that are left blank**

All on `_course_milestone.html.erb` / `_course_activity.html.erb` and the
course-plan show page.

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] Milestone heading is visibly bolder and larger than activity text.
- [ ] The course / round context line renders light grey.
- [ ] The milestone is the second box and expands to reveal its activities.
- [ ] Move up / Move down / Delete sit right-aligned in their row.
- [ ] "Add Activity" both adds an activity and expands/collapses the list. The
      add form is currently always expanded — it should collapse by default.
- [ ] A new course plan seeds one empty milestone with two empty activities.
- [ ] Seeded blanks do not trip required-field validation before the contractor
      has typed anything, and do not count toward the minutes total.
- [ ] Type styles come from the design system —
      `docs/ralph-workflow-policy/design-system-policy.md`, gate
      `script/design_system_guard.sh`. No ad-hoc font sizes or hex greys.
- [ ] Controls keep their 44px minimum touch target.

### 6. Minutes must meet the course requirement

> **Minutes for activities will equate or surpass total number of minutes
> required for course**

Activity minutes and the plan total already exist. **The only missing piece is
the course-level requirement** — `courses` has no such column.

**Decision: add `courses.required_minutes` (integer, nullable). Warn while
drafting; block at submit-for-approval. Null means no requirement and no gate.**
The requirement belongs to the course, not to one contractor's plan — if each
plan set its own target the constraint would be self-certifying. Blocking every
save would make incremental plan building impossible, so enforcement lands at
the submit gate; null keeps existing courses working unchanged.

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] `courses.required_minutes` added, nullable, admin-editable.
- [ ] The plan shows running total vs requirement and the shortfall.
- [ ] `totals_min >= required_minutes` is enforced on submit-for-approval;
      short plans are blocked with a message naming the shortfall.
- [ ] Draft saves are never blocked by this rule.
- [ ] `required_minutes IS NULL` → no warning, no gate.
- [ ] Comparison uses `CoursePlan#recompute_totals!` / `totals_min` — do not
      introduce a second summation with different `synthesis` handling.

### 7. Student tab date filter

> **Under student tab have a date filter which allows contractor to select a
> date and student in order to approve work done while student was absent or
> other instances.**

Lives under `app/views/staff/students/`.

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] Filter selects a date **and** a student.
- [ ] From the filtered view the contractor can approve work for that date.
- [ ] Approval is scoped to the contractor's assigned courses — reuse the
      existing `ContractorCourseAssignment` authorisation, do not widen it.
- [ ] Backdated approval is attributable: it records who approved, when, and
      the date approved *for*.

## Open risks

- **Screenshots not machine-readable here.** Items 3 and 5 were written from the
  surrounding text. Confirm the exact watermark field and type targets against
  Screenshot A/B before editing.
- **Item 1's truncated clause** may have named a fourth symptom beyond the three
  diagnosed. The three above are confirmed in code; if a fourth shows up, report
  it rather than folding it in silently.
- **Item 4 is the largest item** — three input modes, ten slots, upload and
  dictation handling. If it needs splitting, split it and say so.

## Constraints

- Follow `docs/ralph-workflow-policy/` — `design-system-policy.md` for view
  work, `testing-policy.md` before tests, `typechecking-policy.md` for typed
  code (this codebase is `# typed: strict` Sorbet), `security-policy.md` for new
  input surfaces, `verification-policy.md` before reporting completion.
- Never touch production key material: `.kamal/app_secrets/`, `.kamal/secrets`,
  `.kamal/app_secrets.fingerprints`, `script/prod_secrets_*`, or the
  `PROD-SECRET-GUARD` regions in `Dockerfile` and `config/application.rb`.
- `make verify` is the gate. `make help` lists per-gate targets.

- [PA-001] Rewrite the S-1 Turbo-frame bullet and its Files/tests list to require the chosen all-live-frame lock-version refresh in both controllers, then prove two distinct existing frames mutate successfully without reload.

# plan artifact format

A plan is one readable Markdown document. Use the structure that makes the
work clearest; headings and step IDs are optional unless a downstream reader
uses them. Keep it short enough to reread, and state each commitment once next
to the work it describes.

## The only blocking rule

`PLAN001` is the sole error. It means the submission is not a plan: it is
empty or markup-only, has fewer than 100 characters of actual content, is
recognizably truncated (an unterminated frontmatter block, unclosed code fence,
dangling plan field label, final comma or function word, unclosed inline
bracket/parenthesis/backtick, or empty list bullet at EOF), or is clearly a
refusal, question, status update,
tool output, stack trace, or placeholder. Analysis and execution cannot proceed
without a plan to read.

Every other finding is advisory:

- **Warning** predicts a concrete cost to this run and says how to resolve it.
- **Info** is an observation worth a second look.

Warnings and info never make a plan invalid. If proceeding is the informed
choice, record the reason under `## Validation Overrides` as
`- [RULE-ID] reason`. Override reasons remain visible in tool responses and
plan history; stale overrides are reported as info.

## Useful default shape

A good plan normally makes four phases visible in the order they will happen:
Orient, Characterize current behavior, Change, and Verify. It should state the
outcome, real files or areas already inspected, risks or unknowns, and
completion evidence. These are authoring guidance, not required headings.

```markdown
---
type: plan
---
## Work

### [S-1] Characterize the current retry behavior
Inspect the current default and add a focused regression that captures it.

Files:
- modify tests/test_retry.py

### [S-2] Change and prove the default
Update the retry implementation and run the focused test.

Files:
- modify ralph/retry.py
Depends on: S-1
Verify: pytest tests/test_retry.py -q
Expect: the focused retry tests pass with exit code 0
```

Custom headings, prose plans, and an omitted conventional section are valid
when the plan remains understandable. For a larger conventional sample, see
`.agent/artifact-formats/examples/plan.md`. For parallel work, use `## Work Units`
or `## Parallel Plan` only when the executor will consume those markers;
otherwise describe independent work naturally.

## Standard artifact tools

Submit a complete document with `ralph_submit_md_artifact` using
`artifact_type: plan`; `ralph_verify_md_artifact` previews the same result.
For a similar revision, use `ralph_edit_md_artifact` on the staged draft. It
submits automatically when the edited draft has no errors. Use
`ralph_stage_md_artifact` with `mode="replace_all"` only for a wholesale rewrite;
inspect with `ralph_get_md_draft` and submit an assembled draft with
`ralph_finalize_md_artifact`. Staging is not submission: a retained draft that
differs from the canonical document blocks phase completion until it is
resubmitted or deliberately abandoned with `ralph_discard_md_draft`.

Do not write `.agent/artifacts/plan.md` directly. After a valid submission,
call `declare_complete` as the final action.

# typed: strict

class CoursePlanMilestonesController < ApplicationController
  extend T::Sig

  before_action :load_course_plan
  before_action :load_milestone, only: %i[update destroy reorder]
  around_action :lock_course_plan_for_mutation
  rescue_from ActiveRecord::StaleObjectError, with: :render_stale_plan

  sig { void }
  def create
    course_plan = T.must(@course_plan)
    milestone = course_plan.course_plan_milestones.build(milestone_params.merge(position: next_position))

    if milestone.save
      respond_to_milestone_mutation(course_plan, milestone, "Milestone added.")
    elsif turbo_frame_request?
      render_milestone_errors(course_plan, milestone)
    else
      flash[:course_plan_milestone_title_attempt] = milestone.title.to_s
      redirect_to support_course_plan_path(course_plan), alert: milestone.errors.full_messages.to_sentence
    end
  end

  sig { void }
  def update
    course_plan = T.must(@course_plan)
    milestone = T.must(@milestone)
    milestone.assign_attributes(milestone_params)

    if milestone.save
      respond_to_milestone_mutation(course_plan, milestone, "Milestone updated.")
    elsif turbo_frame_request?
      render_milestone_errors(course_plan, milestone)
    else
      redirect_to support_course_plan_path(course_plan, anchor: "course-plan-milestone-#{milestone.id}"), alert: milestone.errors.full_messages.to_sentence
    end
  end

  sig { void }
  def destroy
    course_plan = T.must(@course_plan)
    milestone = T.must(@milestone)
    discarded_at = Time.current
    milestone.update!(discarded_at:)
    CoursePlanActivity.where(course_plan_milestone_id: milestone.id, discarded_at: nil).update_all(discarded_at:, cascade_discarded_at: discarded_at)
    course_plan.recompute_totals!
    redirect_to support_course_plan_path(course_plan), notice: "Milestone removed.", alert: nil
  end

  sig { void }
  def restore
    course_plan = T.must(@course_plan)
    milestone = CoursePlanMilestone.unscoped.where(course_plan: course_plan).find_by(id: params[:id], discarded_at: ..Time.current)
    raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound unless milestone

    cascade_marker = milestone.discarded_at
    milestone.update!(discarded_at: nil)
    CoursePlanActivity.where(course_plan_milestone_id: milestone.id, cascade_discarded_at: cascade_marker).update_all(discarded_at: nil, cascade_discarded_at: nil)
    course_plan.course_plan_milestones.reorder(:position, :id).each_with_index do |sibling, index|
      sibling.update_columns(position: index)
    end
    course_plan.recompute_totals!
    redirect_to support_course_plan_path(course_plan, anchor: "course-plan-milestone-#{milestone.id}"), notice: "Milestone restored."
  end


  sig { void }
  def reorder
    course_plan = T.must(@course_plan)
    milestone = T.must(@milestone)
    reorder_milestones!(milestone, requested_position)
    redirect_to support_course_plan_path(course_plan, anchor: "course-plan-milestone-#{milestone.id}"), notice: "Milestone reordered."
  end

  private

  sig { void }
  def load_course_plan
    @course_plan = T.let(authorize_course_plan(params[:course_plan_id]), T.nilable(CoursePlan))
    course_plan = @course_plan
    raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound unless course_plan && (course_plan.draft? || course_plan.needs_revision?)
  end

  sig { void }
  def verify_course_plan_lock
    raw_lock_version = params[:lock_version].to_s
    course_plan = T.must(@course_plan)
    # DA-006 — a missing or empty lock_version is rejected for
    # EVERY mutation, including create/destroy/reorder/duplicate/
    # reassign/restore. The prior "skip when empty and not
    # update" exception let stale create/destroy requests race in
    # against the latest plan and overwrite newer edits; we now
    # require the parent lock version on every child write.
    if raw_lock_version.empty?
      raise ActiveRecord::StaleObjectError.new(course_plan, action_name.to_s)
    end
    raise ActiveRecord::StaleObjectError.new(course_plan, action_name.to_s) unless raw_lock_version.match?(/\A\d+\z/) && raw_lock_version.to_i == course_plan.lock_version
  end

  sig { params(action: T.proc.void).void }
  def lock_course_plan_for_mutation(&action)
    course_plan = T.must(@course_plan)
    course_plan.with_lock do
      verify_course_plan_lock
      initial_lock_version = course_plan.lock_version
      action.call
      course_plan.reload
      course_plan.touch if (response.successful? || response.redirect?) && course_plan.lock_version == initial_lock_version
    end
  end

  sig { void }
  def load_milestone
    @milestone = T.let(T.must(@course_plan).course_plan_milestones.find_by(id: params[:id]), T.nilable(CoursePlanMilestone))
    raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound unless @milestone
  end

  sig { params(id: Object).returns(T.nilable(CoursePlan)) }
  def authorize_course_plan(id)
    actor = current_user || raise(ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound)
    site = current_active_site || raise(ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound)
    return nil unless current_active_role == :con

    CoursePlan.where(site: site, author: actor,
                     course_id: ContractorCourseAssignment.where(contractor_user: actor, site: site).select(:course_id)).find_by(id: id)
  end

  sig { returns(Integer) }
  def next_position
    T.must(@course_plan).course_plan_milestones.maximum(:position).to_i + 1
  end

  sig { returns(Integer) }
  def requested_position
    raw_position = params[:position].to_s
    raw_position.match?(/\A\d+\z/) ? raw_position.to_i : T.must(@milestone).position
  end

  sig { params(milestone: CoursePlanMilestone, position: Integer).void }

    activity.update!(discarded_at: Time.current, cascade_discarded_at: nil)
    course_plan.recompute_totals!
    redirect_to support_course_plan_path(course_plan), notice: "Activity removed."
  end

  sig { void }
  def restore
    course_plan = T.must(@course_plan)
    milestone = course_plan.course_plan_milestones.find_by(id: params[:milestone_id])
    raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound unless milestone

    activity = CoursePlanActivity.unscoped.where(course_plan: course_plan, course_plan_milestone: milestone).find_by(id: params[:id], discarded_at: ..Time.current)
    raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound unless activity

    activity.update!(discarded_at: nil, cascade_discarded_at: nil)
    milestone.course_plan_activities.reorder(:position, :id).each_with_index do |sibling, index|
      sibling.update_columns(position: index)
    end
    course_plan.recompute_totals!
    redirect_to support_course_plan_path(course_plan, anchor: "course-plan-activity-#{activity.id}"), notice: "Activity restored."
  end

  sig { void }
  def reorder
    course_plan = T.must(@course_plan)
    activity = T.must(@activity)
    reorder_activities!(activity, requested_position)
    course_plan.recompute_totals!
    redirect_to support_course_plan_path(course_plan, anchor: "course-plan-activity-#{activity.id}"), notice: "Activity reordered."
  end

  private

  sig { void }
  def load_course_plan
    actor = current_user || raise(ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound)
    site = current_active_site || raise(ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound)
    raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound unless current_active_role == :con

    scope = CoursePlan.where(
      site: site,
      author: actor,
      course_id: ContractorCourseAssignment.where(contractor_user: actor, site: site).select(:course_id)
    )
    @course_plan = T.let(scope.find_by(id: params[:course_plan_id]), T.nilable(CoursePlan))
    course_plan = @course_plan
    raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound unless course_plan && (course_plan.draft? || course_plan.needs_revision?)
  end

  sig { void }
  def verify_course_plan_lock
    raw_lock_version = params[:lock_version].to_s
    course_plan = T.must(@course_plan)
    # DA-006 — a missing or empty lock_version is rejected for
    # EVERY mutation, including create/destroy/reorder/duplicate/
    # reassign/restore. The prior "skip when empty and not
    # update" exception let stale create/destroy requests race in
    # against the latest plan and overwrite newer edits; we now
    # require the parent lock version on every child write.
    if raw_lock_version.empty?
      raise ActiveRecord::StaleObjectError.new(course_plan, action_name.to_s)
    end
    raise ActiveRecord::StaleObjectError.new(course_plan, action_name.to_s) unless raw_lock_version.match?(/\A\d+\z/) && raw_lock_version.to_i == course_plan.lock_version
  end

  sig { params(action: T.proc.void).void }
  def lock_course_plan_for_mutation(&action)
    course_plan = T.must(@course_plan)
    course_plan.with_lock do
      verify_course_plan_lock
      initial_lock_version = course_plan.lock_version
      action.call
      course_plan.reload
      course_plan.touch if (response.successful? || response.redirect?) && course_plan.lock_version == initial_lock_version
    end
  end

  sig { void }
  def load_milestone
    @milestone = T.let(T.must(@course_plan).course_plan_milestones.find_by(id: params[:milestone_id]), T.nilable(CoursePlanMilestone))
    raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound unless @milestone
  end

  sig { void }
  def load_activity
    @activity = T.let(T.must(@milestone).course_plan_activities.find_by(id: params[:id]), T.nilable(CoursePlanActivity))
    raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound unless @activity
  end

  sig { returns(Integer) }
  def next_position
    T.must(@milestone).course_plan_activities.maximum(:position).to_i + 1
  end

  sig { returns(Integer) }
  def reassignment_milestone_id
    raw_id = params.require(:course_plan_activity).permit(:course_plan_milestone_id)[:course_plan_milestone_id].to_s
    raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound unless raw_id.match?(/\A\d+\z/)

    raw_id.to_i
  end

  sig { params(milestone: CoursePlanMilestone).void }
  def normalize_positions!(milestone)
    milestone.course_plan_activities.reorder(:position, :id).each_with_index do |sibling, index|
      sibling.update_columns(position: index)
    end
  end

  sig { returns(Integer) }
  def requested_position
    raw_position = params[:position].to_s
    raw_position.match?(/\A\d+\z/) ? raw_position.to_i : T.must(@activity).position
  end

  sig { params(activity: CoursePlanActivity, position: Integer).void }
  def reorder_activities!(activity, position)
    activity.class.transaction do
      siblings = T.must(@milestone).course_plan_activities.reorder(:position, :id).to_a
      target = position.clamp(0, siblings.length - 1)
      siblings.delete(activity)
      siblings.insert(target, activity)
      siblings.each_with_index { |sibling, index| sibling.update_columns(position: index) }
    end
  end

  sig { params(_error: ActiveRecord::StaleObjectError).void }
  def render_stale_plan(_error)
    return if performed?

    if turbo_frame_request?
      render partial: "shared/plan_builder/stale_mutation", locals: { course_plan: T.must(@course_plan), frame_id: request.headers.fetch("Turbo-Frame") }, status: :conflict
    else
      redirect_to support_course_plan_path(T.must(@course_plan)), alert: "This plan changed in another session. Reload it and try again.", status: :conflict
    end
  end

  sig { returns(T::Boolean) }
  def turbo_frame_request?
    request.headers["Turbo-Frame"].present?
  end

  sig { params(course_plan: CoursePlan, activity: CoursePlanActivity).void }
  def respond_to_activity_create(course_plan, activity)
    if turbo_frame_request?
      prepare_turbo_success!(course_plan)
      render turbo_stream: turbo_stream_builder.replace(
        "course-plan-milestone-frame-#{T.must(@milestone).id}",
        partial: "shared/plan_builder/course_milestone",
        locals: {
          course_plan:,
          milestone: T.must(@milestone).reload,
          presenter: PlanBuilderPresenter.new(plan: course_plan, variant: :course, current_user: current_user),
          notice: "Activity added."
        }
      )
    else
      redirect_to support_course_plan_path(course_plan, anchor: "course-plan-activity-#{activity.id}"), notice: "Activity added."
    end
  end

  # DA-002 — typed wrapper around `Turbo::Streams::TagBuilder` so Sorbet can
  # resolve the `.replace(...)` call below (the bare `turbo_stream` helper
  # exposed by `Turbo::StreamsHelper` is not on this controller's RBI
  # surface). Mirrors the same pattern in
  # PlanSourceGuidesController#turbo_stream_builder,
  # EvidenceArtifactsController#turbo_stream_builder, and
  # PlanMilestonesController#turbo_stream_builder; it is the single typed
  # boundary for emitting Turbo Streams from any Sorbet-strict controller.
  sig { returns(Turbo::Streams::TagBuilder) }
  def turbo_stream_builder
    Turbo::Streams::TagBuilder.new(view_context)
  end

  sig { params(course_plan: CoursePlan, activity: CoursePlanActivity).void }
  def respond_to_activity_update(course_plan, activity)
    if turbo_frame_request?
      # The returned card becomes the user's next mutation surface. Advance
      # the parent version before rendering it, otherwise its hidden
      # lock_version is stale as soon as the around action touches the plan.
      prepare_turbo_success!(course_plan)
      render partial: "shared/plan_builder/course_activity", locals: { course_plan:, milestone: T.must(@milestone), activity:, presenter: PlanBuilderPresenter.new(plan: course_plan, variant: :course, current_user: current_user), notice: "Activity updated." }
    else
      redirect_to support_course_plan_path(course_plan, anchor: "course-plan-activity-#{activity.id}"), notice: "Activity updated."
    end
  end

  sig { params(course_plan: CoursePlan).void }
  def prepare_turbo_success!(course_plan)
    course_plan.reload
    course_plan.touch
    course_plan.reload
  end

  sig { params(course_plan: CoursePlan, activity: CoursePlanActivity).void }
  def render_activity_update_errors(course_plan, activity)
    render partial: "shared/plan_builder/course_activity", locals: { course_plan:, milestone: T.must(@milestone), activity:, presenter: PlanBuilderPresenter.new(plan: course_plan, variant: :course, current_user: current_user) }, status: :unprocessable_entity
  end

  sig { returns(ActionController::Parameters) }
  def activity_params
    params.require(:course_plan_activity).permit(:title, :description, :time_value_min)
  end
end

      # `Enrollment.where(school_class_id: class_ids)` — which
      # pulled in EVERY student enrolled in any of the viewer's

      # the resolver's `:students` key is the assignment set

      # Enrollment.from(:classes) returned every classmate of
      # every assigned student, not just the contractor's
      # assigned set. The fix uses `scope_hash[:students]`
      # directly, which is the canonical narrowed set for the
      # active (role, site) tuple: self for :stu, assigned set
      # for :con, mentor's class roster for :men, site-wide for
      # :dex, org-wide for :sup. For non-contractor roles this
      # is semantically equivalent to the prior expansion (the
      # resolver computes the same set under the hood) so
      # nothing changes for dean / mentor / super-admin.

      student_ids = scope_hash[:students].pluck(:id)
      class_ids = scope_hash[:classes].pluck(:id)

      current_scope_enrollments = if site
                                    Enrollment.active_on(site.today, site: site).where(
                                      student_id: student_ids,
                                      school_class_id: class_ids
                                    )
      else
                                    Enrollment.none
      end

                               .where(id: current_scope_enrollments.select(:school_class_id))
                               .order(:name)

      # class filter ON TOP OF the resolver-derived set so the contractor
      # assignment set cannot leak to classmates. The base scope is
      # `base_students`; the search narrows it via ILIKE on `users.name`,
      # and the class filter intersects the active set with the set of
      # users currently enrolled in the chosen class.
      if params[:q].present?
        query = params[:q].to_s.first(QUERY_LIMIT)
        like = ActiveRecord::Base.sanitize_sql_like(query)
        base_students = base_students.where("users.name ILIKE ?", "%#{like}%")
      end
      selected_class = nil
      if @roster_filters[:class_id].present?
        selected_class = @class_scope.find_by(id: @roster_filters[:class_id])
        base_students = if selected_class
                          base_students.where(
                            id: current_scope_enrollments
                                .where(school_class_id: selected_class.id)
                                .select(:student_id)
                          )
        else
                          base_students.none
        end
      end

                        .where(student_id: student_ids)
                        .latest_activity_outcomes
                        .to_a

        result[[ submission.student_id, status ]] += 1
      end
      @counts_by_student = student_ids.each_with_object({}) do |sid, acc|
        acc[sid] = {
          approved: counts[[ sid, :approved ]].to_i,
          draft: counts[[ sid, :draft ]].to_i,
          in_review: counts[[ sid, :in_review ]].to_i,
          submitted: counts[[ sid, :submitted ]].to_i,
          needs_revision: counts[[ sid, :needs_revision ]].to_i
        }
      end

      @round = Round.where(site_id: site&.id).current_on(site&.today || Date.current).order(:ends_on).first

      # AC-07 — expose the class-scope dropdown choices and the
      # per-student current-enrollment lookup so the view can render
      # a DayPartTagComponent chip per row. The lookup is narrowed to
      # the active (role, site) student_ids so a contractor never sees
      # an enrollment for a non-assigned student.
      visible_student_ids = @students.pluck(:id)
      visible_enrollments = current_scope_enrollments.where(student_id: visible_student_ids)
      visible_enrollments = visible_enrollments.where(school_class_id: selected_class.id) if selected_class

                                           .includes(school_class: :course)
                                           .to_a
                                           .sort_by do |enrollment|
                                             school_class = T.must(enrollment.school_class)

                                           end
                                           .group_by(&:student_id)

                                          .where(school_class_id: @primary_class_for_summary.id)
                                          .distinct

          school_class_id: @primary_class_for_summary.id

      # no decision a mentor makes changes because seven of their students
      # are AM and five are PM. What a mentor needs from this roster is how
      # much is waiting on them, so that is what we compute instead.
      #
      # Computed over the FULL `student_ids` scope, deliberately BEFORE the
      # pagination below. Summing these in the view would iterate the
      # already-paginated `@students` and silently under-report on any
      # roster larger than one page — precisely the scale at which a mentor
      # most needs the number to be true.

      # Students home (the three-column roster with the role-aware
      # cells). The builder precomputes the per-student
      # participation chip + plan_approval / evidence /
      # final_product cells + waiting totals + breakdowns. The
      # builder excludes example content (Plan#mentor_example =
      # true) from every count, total, and pass membership per
      # §4.15.
      @roster_builder = Reviews::RosterBuilder.new(
        user: current_user,
        site: site,
        role: (current_active_role || :men).to_sym,
        today: site&.today || Date.current,
        class_id: @roster_filters[:class_id].presence&.to_i || selected_class&.id,
        # The name search is a roster filter too. Apply it at the projection
        # boundary (not merely to the legacy @students relation) so every
        # rendered row, count, empty state, and pass origin describes the
        # same narrowed Students list.
        student_id: @roster_filters[:student_id].presence&.to_i,
        round_id: @roster_filters[:round_id].presence&.to_i,
        review_type: @roster_filters[:review_type].presence,
        status: @roster_filters[:status].presence,
        sort: @roster_filters[:sort].presence
      )
      @roster_rows = @roster_builder.rows
      @roster_waiting_totals = @roster_builder.waiting_totals
      @roster_plan_breakdown = @roster_builder.plan_breakdown
      @roster_evidence_breakdown = @roster_builder.evidence_breakdown
      @roster_final_product_breakdown = @roster_builder.final_product_breakdown

      # Rounds for the round-filter dropdown (round phase + date).
      @rounds = site ? Round.where(site_id: site.id).order(starts_on: :asc).to_a : []

      # WT-15 / AC-06 — paged scope + per-page selector so a 200+ student
      # mentor roster does not render as an unbounded 200+ row table.
      # The metric counts (AM / PM / MT) stay above the filter so the
      # operator sees the full population regardless of the page window.
      # The roster renders the projection rows, not the older @students
      # relation. Paginating that relation left later roster rows visible and
      # made the footer a status-only dead end. Page the canonical projection
      # so the visible rows, count, and links describe the same population.
      requested_per_page = params[:per_page].presence&.to_i || PaginationHelper::DEFAULT_PER_PAGE
      requested_per_page = PaginationHelper::DEFAULT_PER_PAGE if requested_per_page < 1
      @per_page = [ requested_per_page, PaginationHelper::MAX_PER_PAGE ].min
      total_count = @roster_rows.size
      total_pages = total_count.zero? ? 1 : (total_count.to_f / @per_page).ceil
      @page = [ [ params[:page].to_i, 1 ].max, total_pages ].min
      offset = (@page - 1) * @per_page
      @roster_rows = @roster_rows.slice(offset, @per_page) || []
      @pagination = {
        records: User.none,
        page: @page,
        per_page: @per_page,
        total_count: total_count,
        total_pages: total_pages
      }
      @student_count = total_count
    end

    private

    sig { params(origin: String).returns(T.nilable(String)) }
    def validated_schedule_origin(origin)
      return signoff_queue_path if origin == signoff_queue_path
      return nil if origin.blank?

      uri = URI.parse(origin)
      return nil unless uri.relative? && uri.path == students_path && uri.fragment.nil?

      pairs = URI.decode_www_form(uri.query.to_s)
      allowed_keys = %w[class_id round_id student_id review_type status sort page per_page].freeze
      return nil unless pairs.all? { |key, value| allowed_keys.include?(key) && value.is_a?(String) }
      return nil unless pairs.map(&:first).uniq.length == pairs.length

      origin
    rescue URI::InvalidURIError, ArgumentError
      nil
    end

    sig { returns(T::Hash[Symbol, String]) }
    def effective_roster_filters
      keys = %w[class_id round_id student_id review_type status sort].freeze
      if params[:clear_filters].present?
        session.delete(:students_roster_filters)
        return {}
      end

      supplied = params.permit(*keys).to_h.compact_blank
      stored = session[:students_roster_filters]
      stored_hash = stored.is_a?(Hash) ? stored.slice(*keys) : {}
      effective = supplied.present? ? supplied : stored_hash
      session[:students_roster_filters] = effective if supplied.present?
      effective.symbolize_keys
    end
  end
end

                                 submission: { activity: { milestone: { round: { plans: :school_class } } } })
                       .ordered

      # DA-005 / S-7 — schedule data for the bounded Student
      # schedule surface: participation by day, activities by
      # day, and the current round.
      @round = Round.where(site_id: site&.id)
                    .current_on(site&.today || Date.current)
                    .order(ends_on: :desc, starts_on: :asc)
                    .first || Round.where(site_id: site&.id).order(starts_on: :asc).first
      participation_scope = if @round && site
                              StudentParticipationDay
                                .where(student_id: student.id, round_id: @round.id, site_id: site.id)
                                .order(:participated_on)
      else
                                StudentParticipationDay.none
      end
      participations = participation_scope.to_a
      @participations_by_day = participations.each_with_object({}) do |p, h|
        h[p.participated_on] = p.day_part
      end

      @activities_by_day =
        if @round
          @activity_records.each_with_object({}) do |activity, h|
            next unless activity.plan&.round_id == @round.id
            start_date = @round.starts_on
            next unless start_date

            # The plan calendar is authoritative whenever an activity
            # has a canonical scheduled day. Older unscheduled rows
            # retain the deterministic position fallback so their
            # schedule remains readable until the programme dean
            # supplies dates.
            date = activity.scheduled_on || (start_date + ((activity.position - 1) / 3))
            h[date] ||= []
            h[date] << activity
          end
        else
          {}
        end
    end

    sig { void }
    def index
      scope_hash = SiteScopeResolver.call(
        T.must(current_user),
        active_role: current_active_role,
        active_site: current_active_site
      )
      # AC (analysis feedback, security regression fix): the prior
      # code re-derived the student list by expanding through
      # `Enrollment.where(school_class_id: class_ids)` — which
      # pulled in EVERY student enrolled in any of the viewer's
      # visible classes. For a contractor this was a real leak:
      # the resolver's `:students` key is the assignment set
      # (ContractorSupport rows at the active site), but
      # `:classes` is the set of classes the contractor's
      # assigned students are enrolled in. Expanding via
      # Enrollment.from(:classes) returned every classmate of
      # every assigned student, not just the contractor's
      # assigned set. The fix uses `scope_hash[:students]`
      # directly, which is the canonical narrowed set for the
      # active (role, site) tuple: self for :stu, assigned set
      # for :con, mentor's class roster for :men, site-wide for
      # :dex, org-wide for :sup. For non-contractor roles this
      # is semantically equivalent to the prior expansion (the
      # resolver computes the same set under the hood) so
      # nothing changes for dean / mentor / super-admin.
      @roster_filters = effective_roster_filters
      student_ids = scope_hash[:students].pluck(:id)
      class_ids = scope_hash[:classes].pluck(:id)
      site = current_active_site
      current_scope_enrollments = if site
                                    Enrollment.active_on(site.today, site: site).where(
                                      student_id: student_ids,
                                      school_class_id: class_ids
                                    )
      else
                                    Enrollment.none
      end
      @class_scope = scope_hash[:classes]
                               .where(id: current_scope_enrollments.select(:school_class_id))
                               .order(:name)

      base_students = User.where(role: :stu, id: student_ids)

      # AC-07 / AC-08 — apply ?q= name-LIKE search + ?class_id=
      # class filter ON TOP OF the resolver-derived set so the contractor
      # assignment set cannot leak to classmates. The base scope is
      # `base_students`; the search narrows it via ILIKE on `users.name`,
      # and the class filter intersects the active set with the set of
      # users currently enrolled in the chosen class.
      if params[:q].present?
        query = params[:q].to_s.first(QUERY_LIMIT)
        like = ActiveRecord::Base.sanitize_sql_like(query)
        base_students = base_students.where("users.name ILIKE ?", "%#{like}%")
      end
      selected_class = nil
      if @roster_filters[:class_id].present?
        selected_class = @class_scope.find_by(id: @roster_filters[:class_id])
        base_students = if selected_class
                          base_students.where(
                            id: current_scope_enrollments
                                .where(school_class_id: selected_class.id)
                                .select(:student_id)
                          )
        else
                          base_students.none
        end
      end

      @students = base_students.includes(:enrollments).order(:name)

      latest_outcomes = scope_hash[:submissions]
                        .where(student_id: student_ids)
                        .latest_activity_outcomes
                        .to_a
      counts = latest_outcomes.each_with_object(Hash.new(0)) do |submission, result|
        status = submission.status.to_sym
        result[[ submission.student_id, status ]] += 1
      end
      @counts_by_student = student_ids.each_with_object({}) do |sid, acc|
        acc[sid] = {
          approved: counts[[ sid, :approved ]].to_i,
          draft: counts[[ sid, :draft ]].to_i,
          in_review: counts[[ sid, :in_review ]].to_i,
          submitted: counts[[ sid, :submitted ]].to_i,
          needs_revision: counts[[ sid, :needs_revision ]].to_i
        }
      end

      @round = Round.where(site_id: site&.id).current_on(site&.today || Date.current).order(:ends_on).first

      # AC-07 — expose the class-scope dropdown choices and the
      # per-student current-enrollment lookup so the view can render
      # a DayPartTagComponent chip per row. The lookup is narrowed to
      # the active (role, site) student_ids so a contractor never sees
      # an enrollment for a non-assigned student.
      visible_student_ids = @students.pluck(:id)
      visible_enrollments = current_scope_enrollments.where(student_id: visible_student_ids)
      visible_enrollments = visible_enrollments.where(school_class_id: selected_class.id) if selected_class
      @current_enrollments_by_student_id = visible_enrollments
                                           .includes(school_class: :course)
                                           .to_a
                                           .sort_by do |enrollment|
                                             school_class = T.must(enrollment.school_class)
                                             [ school_class.name.to_s.downcase, school_class.id, enrollment.id ]
                                           end
                                           .group_by(&:student_id)

      @primary_class_for_summary = @class_scope.where(mentor_id: T.must(current_user).id).first || @class_scope.first
      if @primary_class_for_summary
        @primary_class_enrollment_count = current_scope_enrollments
                                          .where(school_class_id: @primary_class_for_summary.id)
                                          .distinct
                                          .count(:student_id)
        @primary_class_schedule_blocks = ScheduleBlock.where(
          school_class_id: @primary_class_for_summary.id
        ).order(:day_part, :id)
      end

      # The AM / PM / MT metric-card row these counts fed has been removed:
      # no decision a mentor makes changes because seven of their students
      # are AM and five are PM. What a mentor needs from this roster is how
      # much is waiting on them, so that is what we compute instead.
      #
      # Computed over the FULL `student_ids` scope, deliberately BEFORE the
      # pagination below. Summing these in the view would iterate the
      # already-paginated `@students` and silently under-report on any
      # roster larger than one page — precisely the scale at which a mentor
      # most needs the number to be true.
      @waiting_total = @counts_by_student.values.sum { |c| c[:submitted].to_i + c[:in_review].to_i }
      @revision_total = @counts_by_student.values.sum { |c| c[:needs_revision].to_i }

      # WT-09 / S-3 / S-4 — canonical roster builder drives the
      # Students home (the three-column roster with the role-aware
      # cells). The builder precomputes the per-student
      # participation chip + plan_approval / evidence /
      # final_product cells + waiting totals + breakdowns. The
      # builder excludes example content (Plan#mentor_example =
      # true) from every count, total, and pass membership per
      # §4.15.
      @roster_builder = Reviews::RosterBuilder.new(
        user: current_user,
        site: site,
        role: (current_active_role || :men).to_sym,
        today: site&.today || Date.current,
        class_id: @roster_filters[:class_id].presence&.to_i || selected_class&.id,
        # The name search is a roster filter too. Apply it at the projection
        # boundary (not merely to the legacy @students relation) so every
        # rendered row, count, empty state, and pass origin describes the
        # same narrowed Students list.
        student_id: @roster_filters[:student_id].presence&.to_i,
        round_id: @roster_filters[:round_id].presence&.to_i,
        review_type: @roster_filters[:review_type].presence,
        status: @roster_filters[:status].presence,
        sort: @roster_filters[:sort].presence
      )
      @roster_rows = @roster_builder.rows
      @roster_waiting_totals = @roster_builder.waiting_totals
      @roster_plan_breakdown = @roster_builder.plan_breakdown
      @roster_evidence_breakdown = @roster_builder.evidence_breakdown
      @roster_final_product_breakdown = @roster_builder.final_product_breakdown

      # Rounds for the round-filter dropdown (round phase + date).
      @rounds = site ? Round.where(site_id: site.id).order(starts_on: :asc).to_a : []

      # WT-15 / AC-06 — paged scope + per-page selector so a 200+ student
      # mentor roster does not render as an unbounded 200+ row table.
      # The metric counts (AM / PM / MT) stay above the filter so the
      # operator sees the full population regardless of the page window.
      # The roster renders the projection rows, not the older @students
      # relation. Paginating that relation left later roster rows visible and
      # made the footer a status-only dead end. Page the canonical projection
      # so the visible rows, count, and links describe the same population.
      requested_per_page = params[:per_page].presence&.to_i || PaginationHelper::DEFAULT_PER_PAGE
      requested_per_page = PaginationHelper::DEFAULT_PER_PAGE if requested_per_page < 1
      @per_page = [ requested_per_page, PaginationHelper::MAX_PER_PAGE ].min
      total_count = @roster_rows.size
      total_pages = total_count.zero? ? 1 : (total_count.to_f / @per_page).ceil
      @page = [ [ params[:page].to_i, 1 ].max, total_pages ].min
      offset = (@page - 1) * @per_page
      @roster_rows = @roster_rows.slice(offset, @per_page) || []
      @pagination = {
        records: User.none,
        page: @page,
        per_page: @per_page,
        total_count: total_count,
        total_pages: total_pages
      }
      @student_count = total_count
    end

    private

    sig { params(origin: String).returns(T.nilable(String)) }
    def validated_schedule_origin(origin)
      return signoff_queue_path if origin == signoff_queue_path
      return nil if origin.blank?

      uri = URI.parse(origin)
      return nil unless uri.relative? && uri.path == students_path && uri.fragment.nil?

      pairs = URI.decode_www_form(uri.query.to_s)
      allowed_keys = %w[class_id round_id student_id review_type status sort page per_page].freeze
      return nil unless pairs.all? { |key, value| allowed_keys.include?(key) && value.is_a?(String) }
      return nil unless pairs.map(&:first).uniq.length == pairs.length

      origin
    rescue URI::InvalidURIError, ArgumentError
      nil
    end

    sig { returns(T::Hash[Symbol, String]) }
    def effective_roster_filters
      keys = %w[class_id round_id student_id review_type status sort].freeze
      if params[:clear_filters].present?
        session.delete(:students_roster_filters)
        return {}
      end

      supplied = params.permit(*keys).to_h.compact_blank
      stored = session[:students_roster_filters]
      stored_hash = stored.is_a?(Hash) ? stored.slice(*keys) : {}
      effective = supplied.present? ? supplied : stored_hash
      session[:students_roster_filters] = effective if supplied.present?
      effective.symbolize_keys
    end
  end
end
